en.q:
Phosphoric acid ionizes in three steps with their ionization constant values Ka1, Ka2 and Ka3, respectively, while K is the overall ionization constant. Which of the following statements are true?
A. log K = log Ka1 + log Ka2 + log Ka3
B. H3PO4 is a stronger acid than H2PO4− and HPO42−.
C. Ka1 > Ka2 > Ka3
D. Ka1 = (Ka3 + Ka2)/2
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
en.sol:
• A ✓ the overall K = Ka1 × Ka2 × Ka3, so log K is the sum of the logs.
  • B ✓ each successive proton is harder to remove from a more negative ion.
  • C ✓ Ka1 > Ka2 > Ka3 (NCERT §6.11.6).
  • D ✗ no such relation.

Answer: A, B and C only.
en.hint: Overall constant = product of stepwise constants.

hi.q:

A. log K = log Ka1 + log Ka2 + log Ka3
B. H3PO4, H2PO4− और HPO42− से प्रबल अम्ल है।
C. Ka1 > Ka2 > Ka3
D. Ka1 = (Ka3 + Ka2)/2
नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:
hi.sol:
• A ✓ समग्र K = Ka1 × Ka2 × Ka3, अतः log K लघुगणकों का योग है।
  • B ✓ अधिक ऋणात्मक आयन से हर अगला प्रोटॉन निकालना कठिन होता है।
  • C ✓ Ka1 > Ka2 > Ka3 (NCERT §6.11.6)।
  • D ✗ ऐसा कोई संबंध नहीं।

उत्तर: केवल A, B और C।
hi.hint: समग्र स्थिरांक = चरणबद्ध स्थिरांकों का गुणनफल।

en.q:
For the reaction A(g) ⇌ 2B(g), the backward reaction rate constant is higher than the forward reaction rate constant by a factor of 2500, at 1000 K.
[Given: R = 0.0831 L atm mol−1 K−1]

en.q:
Higher yield of NO in N2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2NO(g) can be obtained at
[ΔH of the reaction = +180.7 kJ mol−1]
A. Higher temperature
B. Lower temperature
C. Higher concentration of N2
D. Higher concentration of O2
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
en.sol:
The forward reaction is endothermic (ΔH = +180.7 kJ mol−1), so higher temperature favours NO (A). Adding a reactant (N2 or O2) shifts equilibrium forward (C, D). Pressure has no effect (Δng = 0).

Answer: A, C, D only.
en.hint: Le Chatelier: heat is a 'reactant' for an endothermic reaction.

A. उच्च ताप
B. निम्न ताप
C. N2 की उच्च सांद्रता
D. O2 की उच्च सांद्रता

en.q: For the reaction, 2A ⇌ B + C, K<sub>C</sub> = 4 × 10<sup>−3</sup>. At a given time, the composition of reaction mixture is: [A] = [B] = [C] = 2 × 10<sup>−3</sup> M. Then, which of the following is correct?
o: Reaction has a tendency to go in forward direction.
Reaction has a tendency to go in backward direction.
Reaction has gone to completion in forward direction.
en.sol: Qc = [B][C]/[A]2 = (2 × 10−3)2/(2 × 10−3)2 = 1. Qc (1) > Kc (4 × 10−3), so the reaction moves backward to reach equilibrium.
en.hint: Compare Q<sub>c</sub> with K<sub>c</sub>.

en.q:
Statement I : Acid strength increases in the order given as HF << HCl << HBr << HI.
Statement II : As the size of the elements F, Cl, Br, I increases down the group, the bond strength of HF, HCl, HBr and HI decreases and so the acid strength increases.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
Both statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I : correct but statement II is false
en.sol: Down group 17 the H–X bond gets longer and weaker, so H+ is released more easily: HF << HCl << HBr << HI (NCERT §6.11.7). Statement II gives the correct reason. Both true.
en.hint: Bond strength, not electronegativity, decides acid strength down a group.

en.q: The pH of the solution containing 50 mL each of 0.10 M sodium acetate and 0.01 M acetic acid is [Given pK<sub>a</sub> of CH<sub>3</sub>COOH = 4.57]
en.sol:
Acetic acid + sodium acetate is an acidic buffer. Equal volumes, so the ratio of concentrations stays 0.10 : 0.01.

pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]) = 4.57 + log(0.10/0.01) = 4.57 + 1 = 5.57.
en.hint: Henderson–Hasselbalch equation.
